record_notes.DCP-LETT-1773: November 6, supplied 1855. Returns Journal of Horticulture after reading Decaisne review of Van Mons, distinct from the Gardeners Chronicle review of Flora Indica in P2. Editorial summary conflates those reviews; primary body keeps them separate. Questions usefulness of renaming forms as subspecies unless descent is proved. Asks again for Norwegian seed names and wishes Hooker settled at Kew. Hooker identifications written at head, quoted in footnote, are a separate author contribution with no established sending/receipt day. Earlier 1742 is Darwin own request, not an incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1774: November 8 with supplied month/year. P1 unidentified seed returned by Hooker is distinct from P9 note giving names of the two Norwegian seeds. Darwin only presumes the returned seed dead or not worth planting; not verified viability. Requests Miquel loan to recalculate Candolle and asks Boreau size. Postscript explicitly says identification note just received, allowing November 8 receipt event for that missing note without inventing its body. Reports nine pigeon varieties and reluctance to kill them. Indian Flora scheme and self-revision of Decaisne objection reflect additional missing correspondence. Later 1870 revival is editorial future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1781: November 14, supplied 1855. Thanks missing information on requested books, makes purchase conditional on price. Believes reported old raspberry seeds but distinguishes sixty from two thousand years and is uncertain about chemical change. Rejects Bentham proposed soil search as difficult and inconclusive, not as a failed performed experiment. Asks whether plants become social after introduction and proposes conditional explanatory value of such cases; later notes saying Hooker and Bentham say yes cannot be projected into this question. Penultimate missing Hooker note reported improved baby; Wollaston return with almost eleven thousand insects is reported news. 1774 is an outgoing enquiry, not this reply input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1785: Conjectured November 23, 1855, original Friday morning. A possible Lindley invitation is conditional on health, council duties, time and social familiarity. Darwin would like to go but anticipates possible inability; later nonattendance at council is not already a fact. Differences over charlock evidence are explicitly personal scientific disagreement, not acceptance of Hooker view. Missing invitation/discussion note prevents a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1736: December 9 with supplied month/year despite low document number. Responds to Hooker published December 8 report, which praised charlock evidence while retaining moisture-resistance doubts, and to Loranthus deception example. Only excerpts of that publication occur in apparatus, not full original incoming source. Proposes seed burial in a public garden for long-term records, alternatively his own plot at nine inches with brick sides; experiment is not already begun. Ten-year horizon and stated future age are source prose, not a new exact dateline. Seemann memorandum is unlocated; meeting discussion prospective.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1741: Explicit prior primary reading reused with accepted batch-05 note/ledger and source pins. August 14 with supplied month/year. A new Gray letter/enclosed Hooker note arrived this morning, but that letter is missing; it corrects prior expected proof sheets to manuscript list. Do not treat June 30 source as this morning arrival. Requests Manual loan and names three Erfurt growers matching Cattell August 13, seeking advice on separation and selection rather than trade. Flora Indica almost finished, not completed. Later Natural selection barnacle narrative is quoted apparatus, not part of this letter. Lindley missed visit remains a regret.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1763: Explicit prior primary reading reused with accepted batch-05 note/ledger and source pins. Explicit prior primary full reading reused with accepted note/ledger and matching source pins. Additional full reading, October 10 supplied 1855. Mrs Hooker supplies return/move news, not necessarily a Joseph Hooker incoming letter. Seeds from Kew arrived about ten to fourteen days earlier and are distinct from the two Norwegian seeds. Darwin explicitly has the latter and plans ten-day flotation followed by naming and planting at Kew; those stages are not complete on this evidence. Capsicum/celery germinated after 137 days. Glasgow letter remains missing, Gourlie kindness is a remembered event, and Candolle is being read rather than necessarily finished. This proves Crowe seed-shipment information was known by October 10, earlier than the November direct reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1742: Explicit prior primary reading reused with accepted batch-05 note/ledger and source pins. October 18 with supplied month/year, Thursday evening. Sends two Norwegian seeds from Lofoten and Alten, says they floated ten days, asks naming and planting. This advances his October 10 plan but both letters are Darwin outgoing, not a Q/A pair. Ten-day claim is preserved without inventing an exact experimental start date from approximate sequence. P3 thanks a missing interesting Hooker letter. Hooker names Mucuna and Entada scandens question-mark written at head are quoted by editor, separate from Darwin text. Club attendance is prospective.
